description: Why are ACL injuries so common in women's football? Explore FIFPRO's Project ACL, which investigates potential injury risk factors and how research could help prevent serious injuries and protect players' careers.
question: Evaluate the extent to which ACL injuries in women's football could be reduced through changes to training, player workload and injury prevention strategies. Which approach would you prioritise, and why?
title: Why Are So Many Female Footballers Suffering ACL Injuries?

description: Explore how the heart responds to exercise and why cardiovascular function matters for sporting performance.
question: Explain how heart rate changes during exercise and why.
subtopic: D4 Responses to a single sport or exercise session
title: How Does Exercise Affect Heart Rate?

description: English football generates over £9 billion, yet 94% of clubs are losing money. Discover why rising costs, debt and reliance on wealthy owners threaten the future of football clubs.
question: If you were advising a financially struggling football club, what changes would you recommend to improve its financial sustainability without damaging its competitiveness? Justify your decisions using evidence from the report.
subtopic: E1 Financing a business in sport and active leisure
title: Football Is Worth £9 Billion. So Why Are Clubs Going Broke?

description: Women's football is reaching beyond traditional fans. Discover how the WSL's Interception campaign uses social media creators and unexpected collaborations to attract new audiences and grow the women's game.
question: Evaluate whether collaborating with social media influencers is a more effective marketing strategy for the WSL than traditional advertising. How could the league measure its success?
title: Can TikTok Turn Women's Football into Big Business?

description: NBA hopefuls are tested on their explosive power before the draft. Discover the highest vertical jumps ever recorded and explore how fitness testing helps assess athletic performance.
question: Evaluate how useful the vertical jump test is when assessing a basketball player's potential. Could a player with a lower jump score still be more successful? Justify your answer.
subtopic: B2 Fitness tests to assess components of skill-related fitness
title: Can You Jump Higher Than an NBA Star?

description: Can you trust your smartwatch during exercise? Researchers compared heart-rate monitors and found accuracy decreased during intense movements. Discover how sensor placement affects results and why accurate data matters in sport.
question: Evaluate whether a coach should rely on smartwatch heart-rate data to monitor training intensity. How might inaccurate readings influence training decisions?
title: Is Your Smartwatch Lying About Your Heart Rate?

question: Arteta's furious dressing-room reaction raises questions about coaching behaviour. Explore how communication, motivation and emotional control can influence player relationships, confidence and performance.
subtopic: A1 Skills and knowledge for coaching for performance
title: Does Shouting Make You a Better Coach?

question: Analyse why an elite gymnast might suddenly struggle to perform a previously mastered skill. How could a coach help them regain confidence and control?
title: How Can an Olympic Champion Forget How to Twist?

description: Eddie Hall lifted an astonishing 500kg. Discover the extreme training, recovery and nutritional demands behind his achievement, and question whether becoming the strongest is worth the potential health risks.
question: Evaluate whether Eddie Hall's approach to training and recovery was appropriate for his sporting goals. Would the same methods be suitable for other athletes?
subtopic: D2 Training methods for physical fitness-related components — muscular strength
title: Is Lifting 500kg Worth Risking Your Health?
unit: Unit 2: Fitness Training and Programming for Health, Sport and Well-being

description: Two Olympic high jumpers chose to share gold rather than compete in a jump-off. Explore sportsmanship, decision-making and whether winning should always be an athlete's ultimate priority.
question: Evaluate whether sharing an Olympic gold medal demonstrates positive leadership and sporting values or undermines the purpose of elite competition.
subtopic: Characteristics and qualities of effective leadership
title: Would You Share an Olympic Gold Medal?
